messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T03:20Z for feature flag `ff_route_v2` started against eu-west-1 (canary=5%). Metric watch: initial higher 5xx than baseline (>3x). https://deploys.redwood/internal/rollouts/2179999999 :eyes:

maria (oncall): seeing 502/503s on proxy layer, 3xx -> 5xx ratio up. alert: api.error_rate.eu-west > 2.5% (slo 0.5%). tagging oncall. paging if >4x for 5m :ambulance:

samir (engineer): confirmed. logs show model backend returning ERR_FRAME for streaming shards. pasted a recent trace: `stream_handler.go:178: write tcp: connection reset by peer` — looks like new routing to v2 variant causes backlog. removing canary might help.

jessica (sre): can we flip flag to off? `ffctl set ff_route_v2 false --env eu-west-1` — i can run if the flag service is healthy. what is propagation latency?

samir (engineer): propagation ~30s usually but we have queued requests; if we flip, new requests should hit v1. running `ffctl` now.

samir (engineer): (runs) `ffctl set ff_route_v2 false --env eu-west-1` -> API 200 but service report shows still 85% traffic to v2 for a minute. flag cache TTL maybe 60s.

incident-bot: Paging: oncall escalation to primary oncall (maria). Severity: sev2. Pager duty: notified.

maria (oncall): ok — hold. start short-term mitigation: 1) pin routing to fallback-model (v1-beta) at gateway for eu-west; 2) increase worker concurrency for stream proxies by +2; 3) enable traffic-shed to non-critical tenants. kevin, can you apply route override?

kevin (prod eng): on it. applying gateway override: `curl -XPOST https://gateway.internal/overrides -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","route":"/v1/generate","target":"fallback-v1"}'` — override accepted, verifying traffic.

deploy-bot: Gateway override applied. samples: 90% requests now routed to fallback-v1.

alice (pm): any customer-facing impact? we have a high-volume customer in eu-west on dedicated capacity, will they see errors or latency?

maria (oncall): early estimate: ~6% of total hosted traffic affected, concentrated on chat streaming for small customers; dedicated contracts unaffected (they're on separate pools). Latency increase for affected calls ~+300ms median.

jessica (sre): starting a canary rollback of the v2 image to prior digest (cherry-pick rollback) to remove faulty variant from pool. `deploy rollback --service model-v2 --to 2026-03-14-9f2c` — started.

samir (engineer): deployment rollback progressing, some pods terminating, new pods coming up. watch `kubectl get pods -l app=model-v2 -n eu-west-1` for readiness.

maria (oncall): handoff: i'm stepping out for brief incident coordination with CS. jessica, taking primary. Jess, summarize current actions and keys for next rotation: 1) rollback in progress; 2) gateway override active; 3) monitor 5xx and latency; 4) final confirm when model-v2 instances are fully replaced.

jessica (sre): taking it. I have the rollback watch and will confirm when the last old v2 is drained. next update in ~5m or earlier if anything changes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Handoff: maria -> jessica at 03:26Z. Escalation note attached.

jessica (sre): UPDATE 03:30Z: rollback completed, model-v2 pods now 100% at digest 9f2c, readiness all green. 5xx rate dropping toward baseline (now 0.6% and falling). removing gateway override and reducing proxy concurrency back to normal.

kevin (prod eng): removed gateway override. proxy concurrency set back.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback finished. Metrics: api.error_rate.eu-west=0.45% (below alert), p50 latency delta -220ms vs peak.

jessica (sre): INCIDENT RESOLVED (03:36Z) — services stable. Postmortem owners: samir (root cause triage), kevin (routing/override playbook), maria (oncall ops review). action items: 1) tighten flag cache TTL for edge (reduce to 10s), 2) add automated fallback when model backend returns ERR_FRAME, 3) add runbook step for immediate gateway override. I will create follow-up tasks.

alice (pm): thanks y'all. can we get a short customer note draft for impacted tenants? I'll coordinate comms.

maria (oncall): good job. closing thread once postmortem links added. :thumbsup:
